---
title: "Find out why reticulate picked the wrong Python"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

You call `py_require("numpy")`, and then `import numpy` fails, or `py_config()` shows an interpreter you
never chose. reticulate picks a Python from a list of settings in a fixed order, and an old setting earlier in
the list wins. retiaudit reads those settings **before Python starts**, compares them with what you intend, and
tells you which one is in the way. This page runs it on five situations. Every finding below was produced by
running the code.

## 1. The two questions

```{r}
library(retiaudit)
audit_python(intent = "managed")                                   # I want py_require()
audit_python(intent = "existing", expected = "/path/to/python")    # I want this interpreter
```

`intent` is the one thing the package cannot see for itself, so you say it:

| `intent` | You want | It looks for |
|---|---|---|
| `"managed"` | reticulate to build an environment from `py_require()` | settings that would take precedence over it |
| `"existing"` | a specific interpreter, given in `expected` | a missing interpreter, or settings that point elsewhere |
| `"inspect"` (default) | to see the hints with no intent | only problems that do not depend on intent, for example `RETICULATE_PYTHON` pointing to a file that does not exist (`INVALID_PYTHON_OVERRIDE`, severity `error`) |

It reads a few environment variables, a few project files (whether they exist) and the reticulate version. It
does not load reticulate, start Python or run any file.

## 2. Nothing in the way

```{r}
report <- audit_python(intent = "managed")
report$findings
```

```text
[1] code     severity message  action
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
```

No finding: `print(report)` says *No visible conflict detected. This does not establish that Python will work.*
The check sees settings, not whether the environment has your packages.

## 3. An old override blocks the managed environment

`RETICULATE_PYTHON` is the strongest setting. If it is set, `py_require()` has no effect. Here it points to a
placeholder file (the file is never run):

```{r}
placeholder <- tempfile(); file.create(placeholder)
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = placeholder)

report <- audit_python(intent = "managed")
report$findings
```

```text
                              code severity                                                                   message
1 EXPLICIT_OVERRIDE_BLOCKS_MANAGED  warning An explicit interpreter override takes precedence over managed selection.
                                                                                      action
1 In a fresh R session, remove the override or deliberately set RETICULATE_PYTHON='managed'.
```

Each finding has a `code`, a `severity` (`info`, `warning`, `error`), a `message` and an `action`. Here the
action is the fix: remove the variable (look in `.Renviron`, the shell profile or the IDE's project settings),
or set it to `"managed"` on purpose, and start a fresh R session.

## 4. An activated virtual environment

```{r}
Sys.unsetenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON")
Sys.setenv(VIRTUAL_ENV = tempdir())      # what an activated environment looks like

audit_python(intent = "managed")$findings
```

```text
                          code severity                                                                                     message
1 ACTIVATED_ENV_BEFORE_MANAGED  warning An activated virtual environment is a higher-priority selection hint than managed fallback.
                                                                                       action
1 Check terminal or IDE activation; use a fresh session with an intentional selection policy.
```

This is the case where nothing in your R code changed but the terminal or the IDE was started from an activated
environment.

## 5. The interpreter you expect is not there

```{r}
Sys.unsetenv("VIRTUAL_ENV")
audit_python(intent = "existing", expected = "/opt/python/bin/python")$findings
```

```text
                          code severity                                           message                                                   action
1 EXPECTED_INTERPRETER_MISSING    error The expected interpreter is not an existing file. Check the expected interpreter path before using Python.
```

(The same call with a path that exists gives no finding.) This one has severity `error`: the path you gave is
not a file.

## 6. A project that carries its own tooling

```{r}
audit_python(project = "path/to/project", intent = "managed")$findings
```

```text
                  code severity                                                                                         message
1 PROJECT_TOOLING_HINT     info A Poetry or Pipenv marker is present; a corresponding environment can precede managed fallback.
                                                                                                               action
1 Verify the environment using the relevant project tool; marker presence alone does not prove an environment exists.
```

This is what a project with a `pyproject.toml` returns. The file does not prove that a Poetry environment
exists, so the finding is `info`: it asks you to look, it does not say something is wrong. `report$markers` lists
every project file that was checked and whether it is present.

## 7. Share the report

```{r}
writeLines(audit_markdown(report), "python-preflight.md")
```

The Markdown has the intent, the environment hints, the project markers and the findings, ready to paste into
an issue. It **leaves out** the values of the variables (`RETICULATE_PYTHON` appears as `Set: TRUE`, `value
omitted`), local paths, startup-file contents and package requirements, so you can share it. Read it once
before you do.

## 8. What it does not do

It does not find out which Python a later session will start, check that the environment has your packages, or
fix anything. It narrows the question to the settings you can see; the next step is the finding's `action`, and
then a fresh R session.
